name: matplotlib.pyplot.plot
summary: Lines and/or markers through the points: plot(y), plot(x, y), with a format string such as 'r--o'.

examples.code:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
x = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 5)
plt.plot(x, np.sin(x), label='sin')
plt.plot(x, np.cos(x), label='cos')
plt.title('Two waves')
plt.xlabel('x')
plt.legend()
plt.show()
examples.expected: [figure 1: Plot: "Two waves"; line "sin" through 5 points, line "cos" through 5 points; x (x) from -0.3142 to 6.597, y from -1.1 to 1.1]

name: matplotlib.pyplot.bar

name: matplotlib.pyplot.hist
summary: A histogram of the data: counts in bins (bins, range, density, cumulative, histtype); returns (n, bins, patches).

examples.code:

n, bins, _ = plt.hist([1, 2, 2, 3], bins=3)
print(n, bins)
plt.show()

name: matplotlib.pyplot.subplots
summary: A figure and a grid of axes: fig, ax = subplots(), or fig, axs = subplots(nrows, ncols).

examples.code:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 2)
axs[0].plot([1, 4, 9])
axs[1].bar([1, 2], [2, 1])
plt.show()

name: matplotlib.pyplot.axes
summary: A new Axes in the current figure: axes() fills it, axes([left, bottom, width, height]) places one; keywords set Axes properties.

examples.code:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
ax = plt.axes(xlim=(0, 10), ylim=(-2, 2))
ax.plot([0, 5, 10], [0, 1, -1])
plt.show()
examples.expected: [figure 1: Plot: line through 3 points; x from 0 to 10, y from -2 to 2]
